```{r smooth-m-setup, include=FALSE}
study <- "experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_smooth_v032"
result_dir <- file.path(study, "main_summary")
status <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(result_dir, "status.json"))
comparison_validation <- jsonlite::read_json(
  file.path(result_dir, "baseline_comparison_validation.json"))
stopifnot(isTRUE(status$complete), status$completed_method_runs == 180L,
          isTRUE(comparison_validation$validated),
          comparison_validation$paired_datasets == 90L)
design <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(study, "design.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE)
summary <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "summary.csv"))
runs <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "runs.csv"))
comparison <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "baseline_comparison_summary.csv"))
overall <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "baseline_comparison_overall.csv"))
correlation_by_snr <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "initialization_correlations_by_snr.csv"))
correlation_overall <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "initialization_correlations_overall.csv"))
correlation_value <- function(frame, family, relation, snr = NULL) {
  selected <- frame[frame$family == family & frame$relation == relation, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(snr)) selected <- selected[selected$snr == snr, , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1L)
  selected$median_of_dataset_medians
}
format_correlation <- function(family, relation) {
  sprintf("%.4f", correlation_value(correlation_overall, family, relation))
}
method_labels <- c(adaptive = "Adaptive EB", forward = "Uniform + forward")
unresolved_runs <- sum(runs$status != "success")
convergence_sentence <- if (unresolved_runs == 0L) {
  "All **180 method runs** produced converged estimates."
} else {
  sprintf("The study produced converged estimates for **%d of 180 method runs**, with **%d unresolved outcomes** included in the recovery counts.",
          sum(runs$status == "success"), unresolved_runs)
}
adaptive <- overall[overall$method == "adaptive", , drop = FALSE]
forward <- overall[overall$method == "forward", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(adaptive) == 1L, nrow(forward) == 1L,
          adaptive$planned == 90L, forward$planned == 90L)
auto_dir <- file.path(study, "auto_m_v034")
auto_result_dir <- file.path(auto_dir, "summary")
auto_validation <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(auto_dir, "validation.json"))
auto_overall <- read.csv(file.path(auto_result_dir, "overall_summary.csv"))
auto_comparison <- read.csv(file.path(auto_result_dir, "comparison_summary.csv"))
auto_initialization <- read.csv(file.path(auto_result_dir, "initialization_summary.csv"))
auto_runs <- read.csv(file.path(auto_result_dir, "auto_runs.csv"))
stopifnot(isTRUE(auto_validation$complete), nrow(auto_runs) == 90L,
          all(auto_runs$status == "success"), sum(auto_runs$warning_count) == 0L)
auto_adaptive <- auto_overall[auto_overall$method == "auto_adaptive", , drop = FALSE]
old_adaptive <- auto_overall[auto_overall$method == "adaptive", , drop = FALSE]
old_forward <- auto_overall[auto_overall$method == "forward", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(auto_adaptive) == 1L, nrow(old_adaptive) == 1L,
          nrow(old_forward) == 1L)
current_method_labels <- c(
  adaptive = "Original adaptive EB (M = 8)",
  auto_adaptive = "Automatic-M adaptive EB",
  forward = "Uniform + forward"
)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                     out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = paste0(
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(knitr::current_input()), "_files/figure-html/"))
options(knitr.graphics.rel_path = FALSE)
```

## Question

Can an inexpensive nonlinear similarity estimate the number of latent sample
orderings well enough to initialize adaptive empirical Bayes (EB)? We tested
the automatic-$M$ initialization in **MPCurver 0.3.4** on the 90 fixed
datasets in this one-monotone-anchor study.

The new procedure exactly recovers the final effective $M$ in
**`r auto_adaptive$exact`/90** datasets, compared with
**`r old_adaptive$exact`/90** for the original adaptive fit initialized with
eight slots. It gains exact recovery in **`r auto_comparison$gained_exact`**
paired datasets and loses it in **`r auto_comparison$lost_exact`**. Its
accuracy matches uniform-prior forward selection
(**`r old_forward$exact`/90**) while using substantially less computation.

## Simulation design

Each dataset contains **300 samples and 60 features**, arranged in balanced
groups following **3, 4, or 5 independent latent orderings**. This gives 20,
15, or 12 features per ordering. For sample $i$ and feature $j$,

$$X_{ij}=f_j(t_{i,z_j})+\epsilon_{ij},$$

where $z_j$ identifies the feature's ordering and the latent positions are
independent Uniform$(0,1)$ draws. Within each group, the first feature retains
its original monotone trajectory. The other features follow random smooth
mixtures,

$$f_j(t)=\sum_{k=2}^{4}
\frac{a_{jk}\sin(k\pi t)+b_{jk}\cos(k\pi t)}{k^2}.$$

The coefficients $a_{jk}$ and $b_{jk}$ are independent standard normal draws.

We retain draws whose analytic derivative takes both signs on a fixed
1,001-point grid, producing trajectories with peaks and troughs. Each
noiseless feature is centered and scaled to sample variance one. The
monotone anchor preserves a unique direction of progression through the
complete noiseless feature vector.

The variance signal-to-noise ratio is **1, 4, or 16**, with **10 datasets per
condition**. Each modified dataset retains its baseline's latent positions,
feature membership, monotone anchor, and exact Gaussian-noise realization.
The paired comparison therefore changes the shapes of the other trajectories
while preserving these settings. Both estimation methods receive the same
modified input matrix.

## Methods

### Automatic-M adaptive EB in MPCurver 0.3.4

The new fit calls `fit_mpcurve(intrinsic_dim = "auto")`. It computes a
directional nonlinear similarity for every feature pair: one feature is sorted,
the other is regressed on its rank using a natural cubic spline with five fixed
degrees of freedom, and the variance explained is recorded. The symmetric
similarity is the larger of the two directions. Single-linkage clustering then
considers cuts with at most eight groups and rejects any cut containing a group
with fewer than two features. Among the eligible cuts, the selected $M$
maximizes mean silhouette width.

If the selected groups have sizes $d_1,\ldots,d_M$, adaptive EB starts with

$$p(z_j=m)=d_m/60.$$

Thus the similarity cut supplies both a rough count and data-dependent global
assignment probabilities; subsequent EB updates can remove an occupied
ordering. The minimum group size encodes the study's assumption that every
ordering has at least one distinct anchor plus another feature. It also avoids
treating a single smooth or sortable noise feature as an identifiable ordering.
This experiment does not include a separate garbage-feature component.

The new fits use the released **MPCurver 0.3.4** source at commit
`15f2b0bbe5dfa61cd46da5160b2bc251e75a0475`. Isomap is applied
independently within every selected feature group. All other fitting controls match
the original study, including 50 grid positions, second-order random-walk
smoothing with `ridge = 0`, adaptive cell-position priors, one initialization,
annealing from temperature five to one, and estimated feature-specific noise
and smoothness.

### Original MPCurver 0.3.2 procedures

The two original methods use **MPCurver 0.3.2** and coordinate-ascent
variational inference
(CAVI), with the fitting settings of the all-monotone study. These include
50 grid positions, second-order random-walk smoothing with `ridge = 0`,
adaptive cell-position priors, and estimated feature-specific noise and
smoothness. Initialization uses absolute Spearman similarity, single-linkage
feature grouping, and Isomap within each group; a singleton is initialized
by ranking its feature.

- **Adaptive EB** starts with eight ordering slots and estimates their
  assignment-prior weights.
- **Uniform + forward** fixes the assignment prior to $1/M$, starts at
  $M=1$, and adds slots up to eight. It accepts a candidate when its
  converged temperature-one, soft-assignment ELBO improves and stops at the
  first non-improvement.

The reported **effective M** is the number of slots whose mean posterior
feature-assignment probability exceeds $10^{-12}$. Each candidate uses one
initialization and anneals from temperature five to one. Convergence requires
absolute ELBO change divided by $ND$ below $10^{-6}$, with a 10,000-sweep
limit per candidate. The study records a terminal unresolved outcome if a
candidate required for the estimate fails to converge.

### Trajectory shape and initialization

The modified trajectories have lower within-ordering rank correlations,
which explains why the original Spearman-based initialization is difficult.
Across all 90 datasets,
the median within-group absolute Spearman correlation changes from
**`r format_correlation("monotone", "within")`** to
**`r format_correlation("smooth", "within")`**, while the between-group
correlation changes from **`r format_correlation("monotone", "between")`**
to **`r format_correlation("smooth", "between")`**. Correlations of anchors
with other features in their own group change from
**`r format_correlation("monotone", "anchor")`** to
**`r format_correlation("smooth", "anchor")`**. The grouping step therefore
receives a narrower similarity gap between features from the same ordering
and features from different orderings.

```{r smooth-m-initialization-table}
table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(design$snr, function(snr) {
  data.frame(snr = snr,
    within_monotone = correlation_value(correlation_by_snr, "monotone", "within", snr),
    within_smooth = correlation_value(correlation_by_snr, "smooth", "within", snr),
    between_monotone = correlation_value(correlation_by_snr, "monotone", "between", snr),
    between_smooth = correlation_value(correlation_by_snr, "smooth", "between", snr))
}))
names(table) <- c("SNR", "Within: all monotone", "Within: one anchor",
                  "Between: all monotone", "Between: one anchor")
knitr::kable(table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("Absolute Spearman correlations computed from noisy input matrices.",
    "Each value first takes the median over feature pairs within a dataset, then the median across 30 datasets at the labeled SNR (10 repeats for each true M).",
    "Within-group pairs share a true ordering; between-group pairs follow different orderings."))
```

## Recovery of M

The fixed-df spline similarity cut itself estimates the true $M$ in
**`r auto_comparison$similarity_cut_exact`/90** datasets, with
**`r sum(auto_initialization$initial_under)` underestimates** and
**`r sum(auto_initialization$initial_over)` overestimates**. After adaptive EB,
exact recovery is **`r auto_adaptive$exact`/90**, with
**`r auto_adaptive$under` underestimates** and
**`r auto_adaptive$over` overestimates**. This separates what is learned by
the inexpensive similarity cut from changes made by the fitted model.

The original adaptive fit with eight initial slots is exact in only
**`r old_adaptive$exact`/90** datasets. Relative to that fit, the new
initialization gains **`r auto_comparison$gained_exact`** exact recoveries and
loses **`r auto_comparison$lost_exact`**.
Uniform + forward is also exact in **`r old_forward$exact`/90** datasets.

```{r smooth-m-auto-recovery, fig.cap="Exact effective-M recovery for the three procedures on the same one-monotone-anchor datasets. Columns show the generating M. Each point is a proportion out of 10 datasets at the labeled variance SNR; error bars are 95% Wilson intervals. The automatic-M fit uses fixed-df spline variance explained, single linkage, a minimum initial cluster size of two, and adaptive EB."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(auto_result_dir, "exact_recovery_comparison.png")))
```

```{r smooth-m-auto-overall-table}

table$method <- unname(current_method_labels[table$method])
names(table) <- c("Method", "Exact M", "Under", "Over", "Mean ARI",
  "Mean ordering score", "Median seconds", "Warnings")
knitr::kable(table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("Overall results across the same 90 datasets per method.",
    "Exact, under, and over compare effective M with the generating M.",
    "All 270 fits converged."))
```

### Original paired trajectory-shape comparison

The original MPCurver 0.3.2 analysis asked a different question: how replacing
all but one monotone trajectory in each ordering with nonmonotone smooth curves
changes the two pre-existing procedures. Adaptive EB changes from
**`r adaptive$baseline_exact`/90** exact results in the all-monotone setting to
**`r adaptive$smooth_exact`/90** here; uniform + forward changes from
**`r forward$baseline_exact`/90** to **`r forward$smooth_exact`/90**.

```{r smooth-m-baseline-recovery, fig.cap="Original MPCurver 0.3.2 comparison of exact effective-M recovery in the all-monotone and one-monotone-anchor designs. Columns show true M, rows show method, and color identifies trajectory design. Each point is a proportion out of 10 paired datasets; error bars are 95% Wilson intervals."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "baseline_comparison_recovery.png")))
```

## Recovery of the underlying structure

Feature-group recovery uses the adjusted Rand index (ARI), assigning each
feature to the slot with its highest posterior assignment probability.
Ordering recovery matches occupied inferred slots one-to-one to true
orderings by absolute Spearman correlation, allowing axis reversal.
An unmatched true ordering contributes zero to the mean score. The baseline
and modified fits use this same evaluation rule.

Automatic-M adaptive EB has mean feature-partition ARI
**`r sprintf("%.3f", auto_adaptive$mean_ARI)`** and mean ordering score
**`r sprintf("%.3f", auto_adaptive$mean_ordering_recovery)`**. These nearly
match uniform + forward (**`r sprintf("%.3f", old_forward$mean_ARI)`** and
**`r sprintf("%.3f", old_forward$mean_ordering_recovery)`**) and improve on
the original adaptive fit (**`r sprintf("%.3f", old_adaptive$mean_ARI)`** and
**`r sprintf("%.3f", old_adaptive$mean_ordering_recovery)`**). Relative to
the original adaptive method, the mean paired gains are
**`r sprintf("%.3f", auto_comparison$mean_delta_ARI)`** in ARI and
**`r sprintf("%.3f", auto_comparison$mean_delta_ordering_recovery)`** in
ordering score.

```{r smooth-m-auto-structure, fig.cap="Mean feature-partition ARI and matched ordering recovery for the three procedures. Columns identify true M, rows identify the metric, and each point averages 10 datasets at the labeled variance SNR. Ordering recovery is mean absolute Spearman correlation after one-to-one matching, with unmatched true orderings assigned zero."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(auto_result_dir, "structural_recovery_comparison.png")))
```

### Original paired trajectory-shape comparison

Uniform + forward preserves feature grouping closely: mean ARI is
**`r sprintf("%.3f", forward$smooth_mean_ARI)`**, compared with
**`r sprintf("%.3f", forward$baseline_mean_ARI)`** in the all-monotone study.
Its mean ordering score changes from
**`r sprintf("%.3f", forward$baseline_mean_ordering_recovery)`** to
**`r sprintf("%.3f", forward$smooth_mean_ordering_recovery)`**. The ordering
score averages **0.608 at SNR 1** and **0.999 at SNR 16**, showing that
recovering sample positions is more sensitive to noise than recovering the
number of feature groups in this design. Adaptive EB's count losses accompany
larger decreases in both feature grouping and ordering recovery.

```{r smooth-m-structure-table, results='asis'}
table <- overall[, c("method", "baseline_mean_ARI", "smooth_mean_ARI",
  "baseline_mean_ordering_recovery", "smooth_mean_ordering_recovery", "completed_pairs")]
table$method <- unname(method_labels[table$method])
names(table) <- c("Method", "All monotone: ARI", "One anchor: ARI",
  "All monotone: ordering score", "One anchor: ordering score", "Completed pairs")
cat('<div style="overflow-x: auto;">\n')
cat(knitr::kable(table, format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed"', digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Mean structural recovery across datasets, with completed paired outcomes shown. ARI measures feature-group recovery; the ordering score is mean absolute Spearman correlation after one-to-one matching. Each design's mean uses its completed fits."))
cat('\n</div>\n')
```

The top row shows feature-partition ARI and the bottom row shows matched ordering recovery, with zero assigned to unmatched true orderings. Columns identify true M and colors identify method. Each point averages completed pairs at its SNR; the horizontal zero line indicates equal recovery."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "baseline_comparison_structure.png")))
```

## Runtime and convergence

All **270 method runs** across the three procedures converged without fitting
warnings. Automatic-M adaptive EB has a median runtime of
**`r sprintf("%.1f", auto_adaptive$median_seconds)` seconds**, compared with
**`r sprintf("%.1f", old_adaptive$median_seconds)` seconds** for original
adaptive EB and **`r sprintf("%.1f", old_forward$median_seconds)` seconds**
for uniform + forward. Runtime includes initialization and every continuation;
the forward method additionally fits sequential candidates and its stopping
candidate.

```{r smooth-m-runtime, fig.cap="Median single-thread fitting time for each procedure, generating M, and variance SNR. Runtime includes initialization and all continuations; uniform + forward includes all fitted candidates and its stopping candidate. Each condition contains 10 datasets."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(auto_result_dir, "runtime_comparison.png")))
```

## Summary and reproduction

On these fixed datasets, inexpensive fixed-df spline variance explained gives
a useful conservative estimate of $M$. With single linkage and a minimum
cluster size of two, the initial cut is exact in
**`r auto_comparison$similarity_cut_exact`/90** datasets and never
underestimates. Initializing adaptive EB with that count and cluster-size
probabilities raises its final exact recovery from
**`r old_adaptive$exact`/90** to **`r auto_adaptive$exact`/90**, matching the
more expensive forward search while reducing median runtime from
**`r sprintf("%.1f", old_forward$median_seconds)`** to
**`r sprintf("%.1f", auto_adaptive$median_seconds)` seconds**.

This is an intentionally favorable identifiability setting: feature groups are
balanced, every ordering has a monotone anchor, and there are no garbage
features. The minimum cluster-size rule prevents singleton orderings but does
not identify or model garbage. Unbalanced groups, missing anchors, and explicit
noise features require separate evaluation before treating the initializer as
a general estimator of $M$.

The [experiment directory](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/InferOrder/tree/master/experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_smooth_v032)
contains the fixed design and seeds, curve coefficients, input hashes,
saved candidates, result tables, figures, and reproduction scripts. The
original paired study remains frozen at MPCurver 0.3.2. The automatic-$M$
extension under `auto_m_v034/` freezes MPCurver 0.3.4 at commit
`15f2b0bbe5dfa61cd46da5160b2bc251e75a0475` and records its archive SHA-256,
input hashes, package provenance, scheduler job, and strict result validation.
